Cars of at most 75 kW/t (and at most 105 kW for electric and plug-in hybrid cars), for licences issued from 14 December 2024. Exception: an accompanying driver aged 65 or under with a licence held for at least 10 years sits next to you.
Zero alcohol: if you are under 21 or have had your B licence for less than 3 years, you may not drink at all before driving.
Points taken off for offences are doubled in the first 3 years.
Alcohol limit: 0.5 g/l. Above it: fines, points and licence suspension.
Phone in hand while driving: €250 to €1,000, 5 points and 15 days to 2 months' suspension (first offence).
Points licence: you start with 20 points; 2 years without offences give +2 points, up to 30.
Seat belts in every seat. Children under 1.50 m: approved child seat. Under 4: anti-abandonment device.
Overtaking cyclists: leave at least 1.5 m when the road allows it.
E-scooters: helmet compulsory and at most 20 km/h.
In 2025, 2,868 people died on Italian roads (ISTAT-ACI).
Top causes: distraction (15.1%), failing to give way or running a red light (12.6%), speeding (7.8%).
More than half of the victims (53.3%) are motorcyclists, pedestrians and cyclists.
The EU goal is to halve deaths and serious injuries by 2030 and reach almost zero by 2050.
European Union licences stay valid until they expire.
Licences from outside the EU are valid only for 1 year after you become resident in Italy, with an international permit or an official translation.
After 1 year you must convert it, but only if Italy has an agreement with your country; otherwise you must take the exams. Check the official MIT list.
You get the foglio rosa (learner permit): valid 12 months, with 3 attempts at the driving test.
Mandatory driving-school lessons are 8 hours (city, extra-urban/motorway, night, manoeuvres) under Ministerial Decree 294/2025: ask your driving school for details.
